causes.text: In late May 2025 China's leading EV maker BYD offered generous trade-in subsidies and discounts on more than twenty electric models, reducing the starting price of its Seagull hatchback to as low as 55,800 yuan and offering cash incentives for customers to upgrade. The aggressive campaign escalated an ongoing price war in China's auto industry and signaled BYD's intent to capture market share at the expense of profitability.

source_info.title: BYD offers wide-ranging price discounts, raising price war risk in China

effects.text: Following BYD's trade-in subsidies and widespread discounts, shares of Chinese EV makers fell sharply. Reuters reported that Nio and Leapmotor shares closed between 3 percent and 8.5 percent lower on 26 May 2025 as investors feared a margin-crushing price war.

source_info.title: Nio shares tumble amid intensifying price war

causal_reasoning_chain.description: BYD unveiled a comprehensive trade-in program with deep discounts across more than twenty models, lowering entry prices and signaling an intensification of the pricing war in China's EV market.
Investors inferred that smaller competitors such as Nio would either match lower prices or cede share, implying margin pressure and slower progress toward profitability for firms without BYD's scale.
On 2025-05-26, Chinese EV stocks sold off; Nio's shares fell roughly 6.5 percent as markets priced in a protracted price war and weaker near-term margins.

rationale: BYD's aggressive trade-in subsidies and price cuts re-anchored consumer price expectations and intensified rivalry. The market extrapolated margin pressure to competitors lacking similar scale advantages, driving a sector-wide sell-off that included Nio.
counterfactual_analysis: Absent BYD's aggressive incentives, competitive intensity would likely have remained lower, supporting steadier margin expectations for Nio and reducing the likelihood of a sharp price-driven decline in its shares.

adversarial_confounders.text: Global supply-chain constraints in batteries and semiconductors
adversarial_confounders.impact: could independently weigh on EV makers' valuations, contributing to declines unrelated to BYD's pricing actions

adversarial_confounders.text: Contemporaneous weak macro data or risk-off sentiment in Chinese equities
adversarial_confounders.impact: may trigger broader selling pressure that compounds stock moves attributed to the price war

details.commentary: BYD's deep discounts and trade in subsidies escalated an already intense EV price war, signaling that it was willing to sacrifice margins to grab share. For rivals like Nio and Leapmotor, this move increased the threat of being undercut on price and forced investors to reassess how much profitability any player could sustain in such a crowded market.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Demand environment and consumer behavior
details.commentary: China's slowing economy and cautious consumers made it harder to grow volumes without resorting to aggressive promotions and subsidies. Those demand conditions amplified the impact of BYD's campaign, because many buyers were only willing to upgrade if enticed by sizeable discounts, intensifying worries about sector wide margin pressure.

Once one major EV maker cuts prices, others feel compelled to respond to avoid losing volume, which spreads discounting and compresses industry profits. Each new round of promotions teaches customers to wait for deals, reinforcing a vicious cycle that undermines pricing power and explains the swift negative reaction in peers' share prices.
